newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour's Clark says Lange wrong on defections.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour's Clark says Lange wrong on defections.

text.p: New Zealand opposition Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Friday there was no possibility of defections from her party to prop up a conservative National government after the October 12 election.
Her comments came in the wake of statements from retiring former Labour Prime Minister David Lange that Prime Minister Jim Bolger would try to "wheedle" members away to support him.
"I don't think (Lange) intended to throw a spanner in the works," Clark said on a radio talkback show.
"He is more like an independent commentator and he is not running for parliament again. I think he has called it wrong because I don't see anyone who is likely to leave my party.

"Sometimes in my dreams I think, well, maybe after the election if the numbers are tight I could ring (National backbencher) Max Bradford and offer him something, but the truth is it's not going to happen.
"And it's not going to happen with Mr Bolger trying to fish people out of Labour."

"Labour has got every chance now of leading a government working together with the Alliance and New Zealand First -- why would our people want to give up the prospect of serving in that to go and prop up a failed prime minister," Clark asked.

She said the "disgusting process" of MPs changing parties in the lead up to the election was at an end and Labour would promote legislation to require any MP who left a party to resign from parliament. She said economic nationalist New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance were likely to support such a law change.
Turning to coalition arrangements after the election, Clark said there would not be a formal coalition with the Alliance, but Labour would look to it for support.
"We have fenced off their economic policy as being beyond the pale but I'm sure there are a lot of things in labour market policy and social policy we can talk about."
